propositions: Plan review certified tickets with mutually unsatisfiable acceptance criteria across parent and children, with contradictions surfacing only at implementation or verification gates, forcing costly re-review cycles.

The new ac-satisfiability criterion must detect when a ticket's own AC and Scope/Out-of-Scope declarations cannot all hold simultaneously, covering three shapes: universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, and snapshot cardinality.
The G3 child-coverage audit cannot fire because its sibling roster contains only child ids and titles, lacking the acceptance-criteria items needed to discharge the coverage test.

The sibling roster-building expression is duplicated in three independent places (pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, eval_solver.py), requiring consolidation into a single shared builder to maintain consistency across production and eval paths.

The roster must move from per-pairing instructions into the system prompt prefix to avoid square-growth re-transmission and to enable caching, with its token cost included in the parent_tokens estimate.
G3's posture and threshold remain unchanged; deferred posture decision for ac-satisfiability depends on dogfooding data that the consolidated roster-building ensures will be accurate.
